Chapter 2 Refresh: Using R for data and spatial GIS” 2.1 Introduction This worksheet is intended as refresher for your spatial data handling skills in R/RStudio. It is based on Chapter 5 of Brunsdon and Comber (2018) and uses a series of worked examples to illustrate some fundamental and commonly applied operations on data and spatial datasets. Ultimate many of these form the basis of most GIS software. Before we get to this, the first part of the practical reminds you of some data structures and conventions in R. 2.1.1 Data Data are commonly held in tables, with rows representing observations (people, places, dates, or some other object) and columns represent their attributes. Such long format data are the most commonly used and are similar to a standard spreadsheet. You can download and then load some data using the code below. First download some data from a repository (this is actually for Chapter 2 of Comber and Brunsdon (2020)): download.file("http://archive.researchdata.leeds.ac.uk/731/1/ch2.RData", "./ch2.RData", mode = "wb") You should see file called ch2.RData appear in your working directory. You can check where this is by entering getwd(), then load the data and see what is loaded. load("ch2.RData") ls() ## [1] "lsoa" "lsoa_data" References
